scope: Public sources for a representative 200 mm plasma-assisted GaN chamber and for published simulation-versus-measurement test cases per subsystem. sources.title: Simulation and experiment of a dual-temperature zone MBE heater
sources.supports: 4x6-inch platen MBE heater: pyrolytic-graphite Joule plate (emissivity 0.83), PBN board (0.88), Mo platen/backing ring (rough 0.45), polished Mo insulating plates (0.2), polished Ta reflectors (0.1), rough Ta hull (0.5), GaAs substrate (0.8). COMSOL 6.1 electric currents + solid heat transfer + surface-to-surface radiation (hemicube), ~355k elements, steady state, no rotation. Optimised dual zone: inner width LA = 174 mm, outer LB = 20 mm, under-reflector width L = 20 mm, heater-substrate gap H = 15 mm, plate thickness 2 mm. Measurement: Canon 6D through bottom viewport, 660 nm band filter + ND16, 14-bit RAW grey levels calibrated to a Fluke Endurance pyrometer at the substrate centre; stated error +/-2 K. Radial profiles at 863, 923, 983, 1043, 1103 and 1163 K. At 983 K: M-shaped radial profile, radial difference 3.1 K measured vs 3.3 K simulated (max pointwise deviation 0.89 K); surface difference 5.3 K measured vs 3.3 K simulated.
sources.does_not_support: A reproducible geometry: heater meander layout, platen/wafer-pocket layout, hull and cold-trap dimensions and contact conductances are not tabulated. Headline '0.2 % relative error' is relative to absolute temperature; relative to the measured surface temperature spread the model under-predicts by about 40 % (3.3 vs 5.3 K). Measurement uncertainty (+/-2 K) is comparable to the +/-3 K non-uniformity, limiting discrimination between models. GaAs substrate, not GaN-on-Si; 983 K target, below GaN growth temperatures. Data available only as figures; the user decided (2026-09-29) not to contact the authors, so Figs. 14-16 must be digitized.
sources.use: Thermal validation case with limited discriminating power; design analogue for a narrow outer zone (LB = 20 mm) and reflector stack; material-emissivity priors; camera thermometry method for the sensor decision. Reproduction requires stated geometric assumptions.
sources.affiliations: Central South University; The 48th Research Institute of China Electronics Technology Group Corporation (CETC 48), Changsha

sources.title: Design and optimization of a multi-temperature zone heater for enhanced substrate temperature uniformity in large-sized molecular beam epitaxy systems
sources.supports: Simulation plus experiment for a multi-zone heater with reflective and insulating plates in a large multi-substrate MBE system. Reported: three zones reduce substrate temperature difference from 67.3 K to 9.9 K (87.36% uniform area); 3.05 K at 923 K; two reflective plates cut power 31.88% and shell temperature 53.56%. Uniformity scales with heating-plate flattening ratio and inversely with spacing.
sources.does_not_support: Authors, substrate size and measurement method unverified. Multi-substrate platen geometry differs from a single 200 mm wafer.
sources.use: Zone-count and reflector design-study comparison for WP3.

sources.title: A detailed study of the molecular beam flux distribution of MBE effusion sources
sources.supports: Bismuth from graphite crucibles, cylindrical and conical (taper 2.6 deg), aperture D = 16.5 mm; quartz-microbalance scan across +/-48 mm in a plane normal to the crucible axis at R = 115 mm (one case 265 mm). Measured: filling level L/D (Fig. 3), source temperature / rate (Figs. 2, 4), 60 deg inclination at 0.07 and 26.5 A/s (Fig. 5), cylindrical vs conical at L/D = 2 (Fig. 6), 115 vs 265 mm at L/D = 2, 593 C, centre rates 10.0 and 1.9 A/s (Fig. 7). Findings: central ~30 mm plateau independent of L/D, strong fill-level effect outside it; higher rate flattens the profile; inclination effect small up to 60 deg; 1/R^2 holds; intermolecular collisions in the crucible matter above ~0.2 A/s (Knudsen number lambda/D < 12), so collisionless crucible models fail at practical rates. Transfer method to a rotating substrate with a virtual point source at the taper apex; example for VG V80H geometry q = 160 mm, h = 302 mm, 24 deg (Fig. 9).
sources.does_not_support: Tabulated data (figures only; scanned PDF, digitization needed). Bismuth, not Ga or Al. Absolute fluxes only for Fig. 7 centre rates.
sources.use: Source-transport validation: collisionless crucible model against the 0.07 A/s profile; geometric transfer (fit at 115 mm, predict 265 mm); rate dependence as a model-form limit for collisionless kernels; Fig. 9 as a code-to-code check of rotation averaging.
sources.source_locator: Sec. 2 setup and Fig. 1; Figs. 2-7 measured normalized profiles; Fig. 8-9 and equations p.1212 rotating-substrate transfer; Sec. 4

sources.publication: Chinese Journal of Vacuum Science and Technology 45(6), 461-468
sources.source_locator: Table 1; Fig. 7 crucible geometry; Figs. 8-10 base case; Fig. 11 angle scan; Figs. 12-13 distance scan; Fig. 14 crucible shapes; Fig. 16 fill level; Sec. 4
sources.supports: COMSOL free-molecular-flow simulation of an 8-inch vertical MBE layout (HgCdTe context, CdTe source), diffuse crucible walls, rotating substrate. Cylindrical crucible bore 71.5 mm, depth 174 mm (170 mm in Fig. 7), fill depth 140 mm, axis aimed at wafer centre; angle phi measured from the wafer normal (phi = 0 symmetric, Fig. 5). Base 35 deg / 350 mm: centre-peaked rotated profile about 2.66 to 2.41 (x1e15) centre to edge, stated non-uniformity 8.2 %. Angle scan: best at 46 deg. Distance scan at 46 deg: range below 1.4 % beyond 300 mm. Shapes at 40 deg / 350 mm: cylindrical 4.36 %, conical 1.4 %, constricted-neck 2.35 %. Flux falls about linearly with source consumption (slope about -2/3 at centre). Also lists 8-inch-class tools: RIBER MBE8000 (4x8-inch), Veeco GEN2000 (7x6-inch), CETC 48 (4x6-inch).
sources.does_not_support: Measurement: simulation only, so agreement is code-to-code corroboration, not validation. Non-uniformity metric is not defined and does not reproduce exactly from Fig. 10; depth 174 vs 170 mm inconsistency; distance used in the angle scan not stated explicitly (Table 1 gives 350 mm). CdTe, not Ga/Al.
sources.use: Code-to-code comparison for the crucible emission model on an 8-inch geometry: optimum angle near 46 deg, base-case centre-to-edge ratio about 0.90, crucible-shape ranking.
